system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In June 2024, what wording did Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code, as then in force, use to define the limits of punishing a child? Quote the wording.
raw_response:
Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code, as it stood in June 2024 (before the 2024 amendment removing corporal punishment language), empowered a parent to:

**"punish the child in a reasonable manner for disciplinary purposes"** (ทำโทษบุตรตามสมควรเพื่อว่ากล่าวสั่งสอน)

This was the operative wording limiting parental disciplinary power to what was "reasonable" (ตามสมควร) and tied to the purpose of admonition/correction (เพื่อว่ากล่าวสั่งสอน), before Thailand's later reform explicitly banning violent or degrading punishment of children.
